# X (Free Read/Write)

Search and read posts, discover account Lists and read List timelines, manage List members, view user profiles, post text, reply, and delete using cookies from a signed-in X account. No official API key or subscription is required. This plugin uses the open-source TweetKit library and X web endpoints. Free means no official API call fees; self-hosting may still incur server or network costs.

This guide covers the eleven operations in the v0.2.0 contract. This version adds four operations: Get my Lists, Get List posts, Add List member, and Remove List member.

## Configure credentials

1. Sign in normally to an X account you are authorized to use and open `https://x.com`.
2. Open developer tools → Application → Cookies → `https://x.com`.
3. Copy the values of `auth_token` and `ct0` into Login token and CSRF token. Both must come from the same session. Do not paste the whole Cookie header.
4. Optionally configure a proxy reachable by the plugin process. Inside a container, `127.0.0.1` is the container itself; Docker Desktop commonly uses `host.docker.internal` to reach the host.
5. Click Test. This reads a timeline without posting; success confirms this read succeeded, not every possible write permission.

Cookies are login credentials. Keep them in platform credentials, not workflow parameters, logs, or public repositories. This plugin does not log in with a password, solve verification challenges, or rotate accounts.

## Operations

- **Search posts**: use X search syntax such as `from:username keyword` to read recent matches.
- **Get user posts**: enter a username, optionally with `@`, to read recent posts.
- **Get my Lists**: read Lists on the authenticated account's List management page, then select a List by name to obtain its ID.
- **Get List posts**: enter a List link or ID to read one page of posts; use the returned cursor to continue backward through history.
- **Add List member / Remove List member**: enter a List link or ID and a username to manage members of a List you have permission to manage.
- **Get post / Get user profile**: query by post ID or username respectively.
- **Post or reply**: enter text; leave Reply-to post ID empty for a new post, or provide a post ID for a reply.
- **Delete post**: enter an ID the current account can delete. Deletion cannot be undone.

Search posts and Get user posts default to 20 results and accept up to 100; X may return fewer. These two operations return bounded recent batches, without historical archives or pagination cursors across calls. Deduplicate by post ID in scheduled workflows. See below for Get List posts pagination. Check credentials verifies the session and connection with a read-only timeline request, without posting. Media uploads, direct messages, and real-time event triggers are not currently supported.

## Find my Lists

If you do not know the List ID, first select Get my Lists (`my_lists`). This operation uses the authenticated account to read Lists on its X List management page. These can include created and followed Lists, not just Lists the account owns. Select the target by its returned `name`, then pass its `id` to Get List posts.

Each call requests only one page. Provide Requested page size (`limit`, 1 to 100, default 20) and an optional Pagination cursor (`cursor`); leave the cursor empty initially and pass the returned `next_cursor` to continue paging. The plugin returns a complete page, with the actual count determined by X. The returned `lists` includes each List's `id`, `name`, `description`, `mode` (`public` / `private`, or empty when unknown), `member_count`, `subscriber_count`, `owner_id`, `owner_username`, and `url`. The response also includes the actual `count`, `next_cursor`, and `has_more`. An empty page with a cursor can still have more pages. This operation does not create or modify Lists.

## Manage List members

After selecting a target with Get my Lists, use Add List member (`add_list_member`) or Remove List member (`remove_list_member`). Enter List link or ID (`list_id`, in the format described below) and Username (`username`, optionally prefixed with `@`; do not enter a profile URL). The authenticated account must have permission to manage that List. Being able to read a List does not mean you can change its members.

Each operation handles one account at a time; it does not automatically add or remove members in bulk. These operations manage the accounts included in a List; they do not follow or unfollow the List. On success, they return List ID (`list_id`), the target User ID (`user_id`), Username (`username`), and Operation succeeded (`changed`). `changed` means X accepted the operation. It does not establish whether the account was already a member or whether membership changed for the first time.

Failures are not automatically retried; disable automatic retries for these write nodes in workflows too. After a timeout or dropped connection, check the List's membership on X before deciding whether to retry. The plugin does not create Lists; create the List on X first.

## Get List posts

Select Get List posts (`list_timeline`) in your workflow. Use an ID returned by Get my Lists, or enter an existing link or ID directly. Get my Lists and Get List posts are read-only operations and do not change members. Private Lists can only be read when the account associated with the credentials has access.

| Input | Description |
| --- | --- |
| List link or ID (`list_id`) | A numeric ID or `https://x.com/i/lists/<id>`; `https://twitter.com/i/lists/<id>` is also accepted. |
| Requested page size (`limit`) | 1 to 100, default 20. This is the requested page size; X may return more or fewer posts. To avoid skipping data after truncation, the plugin returns the whole page without truncating it to this value. |
| Pagination cursor (`cursor`) | Optional; leave empty for the first request, then pass the previous `next_cursor` from the current run. |

Each call requests only one page and returns these fields:

| Output | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Posts (`posts`) | The complete list of posts parsed from this page. |
| Returned count (`count`) | The number of posts actually returned, which may differ from the requested page size. |
| List ID (`list_id`) | The numeric ID parsed from the input, returned as a string. |
| Next page cursor (`next_cursor`) | A cursor for paging backward through history during the current collection run. |
| Can continue paging (`has_more`) | Whether a usable next-page cursor was returned; this does not guarantee that the next page contains posts. |

An empty page can still contain a next-page cursor. Do not conclude that collection is complete just because `posts` is empty or `count` is 0. A cursor is not a checkpoint for new posts in the next scheduled run; each scheduled run should start with an empty cursor to fetch the latest page again.

## Scheduled List collection

First use Get my Lists to select the target ID by name, then build a workflow using a timer → Get List posts → idempotent data-table writes → additional pages as needed. The following rules reduce duplicates and omissions, but do not guarantee zero missed posts or complete historical coverage.

1. **Choose the initial scope**: on the first run, establish a current baseline or define an explicit historical range. Do not assume the first run should traverse all history.
2. **Start from the latest page**: leave `cursor` empty at the beginning of each scheduled run. A 10–15 minute interval is a configuration starting point, not a guarantee against rate limits; adjust it based on List activity, the number of pages fetched, and X responses.
3. **Write idempotently**: use the returned `list_id` and each post's `id` (stored as `post_id` in the table) as a composite primary key, updating or ignoring duplicates. Store both IDs as strings to avoid losing precision with large integers.
4. **Fetch additional pages within the run**: pass `next_cursor` to the next call to read backward through history. After reaching posts within the last fully completed range, allow a small number of overlapping pages and deduplicate each post by ID. Reposts and out-of-order results can contain unprocessed older IDs, so do not compare only the largest post ID or stop immediately at the first known post. Apply the same rules to empty pages that still have a cursor.
5. **Set bounds and failure alerts**: configure a maximum page count per run and failure notifications. Only mark a run complete and advance its completed checkpoint after reaching the previously processed boundary with the chosen overlap, or when X no longer provides a next-page cursor. If the maximum page count is reached, or a request fails with 429 rate limiting, 401 session expiry, or another error, keep rows already written but do not advance the completed checkpoint. After resolving the issue, restart from the latest page and deduplicate with the composite key so that unprocessed ranges are not skipped.

The checkpoint records the scope of the last fully completed run; it cannot replace per-post ID deduplication in the data table. Partial writes from a failed run must not be treated as a completed boundary. List membership, post visibility, and web endpoints can change, and the endpoint may not expose all historical posts. Do not rely on this operation to guarantee a complete archive.

## Errors and limits

- **Expired session / restricted account**: confirm the account works in your browser, then replace both cookies from the same session.
- **Rate limit**: reduce request frequency and wait for the limit to reset; the plugin does not rotate accounts to bypass limits.
- **Network error**: check whether the plugin process can reach its proxy.
- **No List management permission**: confirm the authenticated account can add or remove members of that List; reading or following a List does not grant management permission.
- **Changed web endpoints**: update the plugin; these endpoints have no official compatibility guarantee and continuous availability is not assured.
- **Posting timeout or dropped connection**: check X for the post before retrying. The plugin does not automatically retry writes; disable workflow-node automatic retries too to avoid duplicate posts.

Web automation can trigger verification, locking, or account restrictions. Start with an authorized test account and a low request rate. No official API subscription does not mean anonymous access or unlimited usage.
